script.stored_text_completeness: All 16980 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 1 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored ending is complete ("It's just math that nobody bothered to explain."); ASR artifacts ("200 $23,800", "Vibe's economy", "Your 2024 Credit Karma study"); 2,851 words over 1,221 seconds (~140 wpm) is consistent with a full read; audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: Two guys, same age, same neighborhood, same mortgage payment, same beat-up Toyota in the driveway, same Tuesday night habit of watching something on Netflix they'll forget by Thursday. One of them opens his investment app after dinner, sees $300,000 staring back at him, and exhales. Feels like he's getting somewhere, like the years of brown bag lunches and skipping vacations finally added up to something real. The other guy opens the exact same app, sees the exact same number, and
script.ending_words: math is the same either way, but only one version of Marcus is making decisions from the right starting point. The number isn't the problem. The problem is that we built an economy where doing everything right for decades still leaves most people feeling like they're one bad year away from losing it, and then we call that feeling irrational. It isn't. It's just math that nobody bothered to explain.
script.analysis: Full 16980 canonical characters read. A perception essay: two reactions to the same $300,000, Marcus and Diane (43, Columbus, $115K), wealth distribution and Musk comparison, Schwab wealth thresholds, inflation erosion, category inflation, home equity vs liquidity, 4% rule and Social Security, Vanguard balances, compounding and critical mass, life shocks (emergency fund, college, long-term care), sandwich generation, sequence risk (2007-09, 2022), money dysmorphia and social comparison, and a reassurance close. Verified: Schwab 2025 $2.3M/$839K; many compounding and sum calculations reproduce. Wrong or inconsistent: 2022 loss ($61,500 at the stated 20.5%, not $76,200); Musk $250B vs "$800 billion in a year"; retirement gap ignores the second spouse's Social Security; compounding applied to the full $300K after excluding home equity; premiums +54% not +49%. The stored ending is complete.
beat_map: 4% rule, Social Security and retiree spending gap.
Vanguard 65+ balance; compounding and critical mass.
Life shocks: emergency fund, college, long-term care.
Reassurance: future value of $300,000 and close.
